verdicts.note: Refers to herself as a 'female engineer'; clearly female.
'Girl's Grammar School' = single sex.
Cited quote is internally muddled, but 'especially the 2nd year because the 1st year was all...' confirms current Year 2.
States 'Mechanical engineering'.
Quote shows interest not ability, but maths/physics A-levels and 'I can guild numbers / very practical' support 'good at'; agree fine.
Quote is about not narrowing to a specific engineering branch (aero/auto), NOT about using science+maths without specialising in either; does not address this construct.
'varied enough... get as much out of it' is the explicit reason she chose mechanical; variety appeal confirmed.
Practical whole-process work appeal supports interesting-work draw.
Dad is in the engineering industry (sales-support, ex-apprentice engineer), so family-in-industry holds; but she heavily downplays his role and never cites him as her route, so thin.
'My Dad was [supportive]' re her choice.
Mother wanted maths/accounting instead; did not encourage engineering = disagree.
Careers people 'backed me up a lot' and were 'really into it'.
Physics teacher 'really excited about it'.
Mother said 'I told you not to do the course' = discouragement occurred.
Mother is the discourager (links to 'my mum wasn't' + 'I told you not to do the course').

Quote is about wanting to be 'slightly more aware of the workload', not lacking knowledge of what engineers do; she actually had extensive prior exposure (2 work placements, insight courses, WES since 16), which cuts against 'agree'. Downgrade.
Quote describes her own collaborative working preference; it does not address whether engineering students are competitive.
Would only research more, otherwise wouldn't change; also 'happy with the career choices' = pleased.
Says group work teaches working with people and handling conflict; her own elaboration carries the affirm.
Group projects named 'the worst thing'; clearly dissatisfied.
Personal tutor approachable and 'quite good' = satisfied.
'Hated... got used to it' is tepid (borderline neutral); positive framing of taking CAD to placement nudges to satisfied but thin.
Quote is about content becoming more interesting/advanced ('more interesting things rather than basic examples'), NOT about the variety/breadth of subjects; does not address this construct.
Quote only evidences dissatisfaction with one bad lecturer; overall 'neither' is an inference (prefers the others). Keep low.
Actively applying, intends to go = yes.
'Gain the experience and just seeing how it does work in the real world'.
'idea of how industry works instead of the classroom' = wants to see industry.
Wants to see which bits she doesn't want / 'knowing where I want to go when I'm finished'.
Says placement shows you're grounded in industry vs just theory = improves job chances; her own elaboration.
'You can apply it, knowing what's needed for what'; interviewer prompted but she elaborates in her own words.
Quote is about wanting the 'real world / be normal again', an indirect mapping to 'need a break from education'; defensible but thin. Downgrade.
'Making new contacts' is networking, only loosely a personal-development reason; thin mapping. Downgrade.

She is pro-placement and dismisses the 'just finish and earn money' view, so the finish-ASAP reason = disagree. Quote is awkward but a clearer one exists ('comments about just doing the 4 years... nothing really serious').
'most interested in... research' and 'Research, hopefully' = research/development.
'I would prefer to stay with research' over managerial = technical/specialist.
Names gaining chartership as a 10-year goal; aspirational positive = important.
Training a 'bonus' but won't drive her choice = neither important nor unimportant.
Evidence quote is the TRAINING quote ('extra training') and does not mention salary at all; quote does not support the salary construct (relevant pay material exists elsewhere but was not cited).
A 'graduate development programme' is vocational on-the-job development, not clearly academic 'further study'; no Masters/PhD mentioned. Thin; downgrade.
